text: Image paste and drag in agent chat

prompt:
New feature: drag or paste (Cmd+V) an image into the message box so the agent can look at it. It works in a new session and in follow-up messages, and shows in the chat after a reload.

In the box:

- Images stand in a row above the text, 8px apart, as 120x120 tiles with 10px corners; the whole image fits, on a dark tile.
- On hover, a small round X on the tile's top-right corner removes it.
- A click opens the image large; X or Esc closes it.

Decide the rest yourself and list your choices in the pull request. Keep the image files on this computer only: not in the checkout, not in the shared agent data. Add tests, test it by hand in a real browser with one real agent run that reads a word from a screenshot, and open a pull request that names no other product.

Exit code 1
## Decisions

- **The CLI always runs in the foreground.** Ctrl-C closes everything — the dashboard and every session it is running. There is no background/detached daemon mode.
- **The CLI options are minimal.** Every other setting belongs to the dashboard, which is the product's only user interface.
- **Only remove what has been pushed to the git remote.** Worktrees, branches, archives — anything OpenAgent removes on its own initiative must already exist on the remote, so every removal is recoverable from it. A delete the user asked for and confirmed is the exception: throwing the work away is what it is for.
- **Never interrupt a running session because of low quota.** Quota gates whether a session may *start*; a session already running is never paused, degraded or cut short.
- **The unit of work is an *agent*** — not a run or a session. The CLI that drives it (`claude`, `codex`) is the *driver*.
- **Zero migration code.** Manual migration is good; code that migrates is not. A renamed or deleted thing leaves nothing behind — no fallback to the old name, no key alias, no old-format branch, no upgrade step. Nor a notice about what was dropped: a warning about data nobody has is still code nobody needs.
- **Haiku is out of scope.** It skips the session-finish protocol, so unattended work started on it always ends as an unmerged draft PR that a human has to finish. We deliberately don't work around this: no model floor that overrides the model a user picked, and no refusal to arm the hand-off. The dashboard's warning is the whole treatment — it teaches and never blocks.
- **The dashboard is a page on `localhost`, not a native app.** The users for now are developers, and `localhost` is what they know. Non-technical users will most likely use the hosted version. A native app (or a local domain) may come later, beside `localhost`.
- **The version line stays in `0.x`.** The releases are experimental, and while the major is `0` a minor bump is allowed to break

I'm weighing how the images should get from the browser to the daemon. One option is to send the raw image bytes over an RPC at paste time, have the daemon save them into a private local directory under a content hash, and pass back an id that the message then carries for the agent to read.

I'm weighing whether the agent driver can take image blocks as base64 directly, or whether pointing it at the saved file path is enough. Claude Code can view images through its Read tool, but passing content blocks is the proper route. Codex takes images through a path flag. Next I want to check how the dashboard's rpc() call works, including whether it sends JSON over HTTP and what size limits apply.

258	export function withTextsApart(args: readonly string[], options: Options): string[] {
259	  const flags: string[] = []
260	  const texts: string[] = []
261	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
262	    const arg = args[i]!
263	    if (arg === '--') {

/**
 * One workspace-bound Codex session. Every `prompt` is its own `codex app-server` process, asked
 * for one turn: on a fresh conversation, or, for a `resume` prompt, on the session's conversation
 * continued.
 */
export class CodexSession implements DriverSession {
  readonly id: string
  readonly cwd: string
  readonly log?: SessionLog
  private readonly startOpts: DriverStartOptions
  /**
   * The conversation a `resume` prompt continues: the one the session was started to resume,
   * then the one the last turn reported. Codex keeps the id across a resume, so consecutive
   * messages chain.
   */
  private lastSessionId: string | undefined
  /** Codex's model list, read once for the session the first time it is needed. */
  private listed: Promise<DriverModel[]> | undefined
  /** The Codex account the session is on, by name, when it runs on accounts: kept until its limit moves it on. */
  private readonly current: { account?: string } = {}

    private readonly config: CodexDriverOptions,
    startOpts: DriverStartOptions,
    /** Codex's models, for the effort one thinks at when none was picked and Codex did not say. */
    private readonly models?: () => Promise<DriverModel[]>,
  ) {
    const attached = attachLog(startOpts)
    this.startOpts = attached.opts
    if (attached.log) this.log = attached.log
    this.cwd = startOpts.cwd
    this.id = `codex-${++sessionCounter}`
    this.lastSessionId = startOpts.resumeSessionId

text:
# End to end

The dashboard as a person meets it, offline. Every project here is a fixture repo (`fixture.ts`),
and its runs are the scripted host's (`fake-runs.ts`): this computer's own host, agent-driver's,
whose runs' processes are `fake-run-bin.ts` in place of `agent-runner run`, a scripted coding agent in
the seat of `claude` or `codex`. A Start goes the whole production way — the dashboard's call, the
host, a detached run writing the files the dashboard reads — and costs nothing. A session with no
project is not scripted: the host refuses it.

A word in the prompt picks what the scripted agent does:

| Word | The run |
|---|---|
| `ask` | asks "Which way?" and waits for the answer |
| `hold` | waits for `<checkout>/.openagent/go` before its first turn, so it is certainly still working |
| `commit` | commits a file, so its branch holds work to push |
| `refuse` | the host refuses it, and the page says why |
| `agents` | its coding agent starts subagents of its own, one of which fails, and it keeps working until it is stopped; with `many`, more of them |
| anything else | answers `done: <prompt>`, and the run ends |

## The backend stories: `story-*.test.ts`

The daemon's own functions, wired as `runDaemon` wires them (`harness.ts`) and called as the page
calls them: what each flow leaves on disk, and what the reads then say. No browser.

## The demo: `pnpm demo`

The real dashboard, started by its built CLI on a throwaway home (`demo.ts`) and handed the
distribution whose host scripts the runs (`distribution.ts`): a project "shop", its tickets,
queue, logs and scheduled-agents plugins switched on, with two skills of its own, two tickets, a
working, a waiting and a done run, and the Logs and Automations pages; and a project "blog" to
add from the picker, whose runs are scripted too, its plugins as a new project's. Walk any flow
by hand. Ctrl+C stops the runs and the dashboard, and removes the home.

## The browser smoke stories: `smoke-*.test.ts`

The demo in Chrome, driven by playwright-core (`smoke.ts`): the flows people go through most,
checked as a person sees them, with the page laid out and run, its calls over HTTP, the host and
the run's files. They need `pnpm build` and a Chrome (`CHROME_PATH`, or one where Chrome usually
is), and are skipped without one. A flow that fails leaves a screenshot in
`packages/ui/test-results/`, which CI keeps.

In a script of your own, `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` never comes: the page keeps a stream to the
daemon open. Wait for `load` and the element you need.

I'm waiting on the explorer's result, but I can't simply pause without ending the turn and handing control back to the user. Since agent completion should re-invoke me, I'll keep making progress on independent work and start on the UI image tiles component. The tiles are 120x120 with rounded corners and a dark background.

Next I'm settling the tile's details: a dark background, rounded corners, and the image fitted inside. The close button sits small and round in the top-right corner, and clicking a tile will open the larger view in a dialog that closes on Escape.

I'm weighing whether images should send with no text at all. I'm leaning toward requiring a message with words, so the agent knows what to do with the screenshot, though I'm keeping image-only sending as an option to revisit.

I'm sketching the composer change next: it needs to hold the images alongside the text, and the clear and restore paths have to carry both, so a failed send puts the screenshots back too.

Checking the other callers of clear and restore to see how the composer's draft gets handed back.

text:
I'm checking whether Claude Code resizes images sent through stream-json input, since it does for pasted images and the Read tool but I'm not sure about this path. To be safe, I'll have the browser normalize images to the API limits: at most 5MB base64 (about 3.75MB raw) and a long edge of 8000 pixels.

I'm weighing whether to downscale images in the browser to a long edge of 2000px, since the API resizes anything over about 1568px anyway and that could lose text detail in large screenshots. I'm leaning toward keeping images as they are when they fit the limits, and only re-encoding to a smaller size when they don't, so the stored copy is the same file the agent sees.

I'm thinking about where image files and references should live: the image files stay out of the checkout, and storing absolute paths in shared data would leak the home directory, so I'd only store ids like sha256.ext there. The daemon serves them from a local directory, and on another machine the tile would show a "Not on this computer" placeholder. Next I want to check the explorer and look at how the prompt is built in claude-code.ts.

 * as the branch it is on — the data branch's persistent checkout beside the agents' own. Dotted
 * on purpose: a `*` glob does not match a leading dot, so type-checkers, test runners and
 * formatters run in the project never descend into N copies of the repository.
 */
export const BRANCHES_DIR = '.branches'

/**
 * The shared data branch of a project: the one branch every skill keeps its files on, a path per
 * skill, checked out once at `.branches/agent-data`. Named here, once, for every consumer to
 * import — never spelled out again.
 */
export const DATA_BRANCH = 'agent-data'

/** Where a clone keeps origin's copy of its branches. */
const ON_ORIGIN = 'refs/remotes/origin/'

/**
 * How a run is told to start from a branch as origin has it, rather than as this clone does: the
 * full name of origin's copy, the one spelling a branch of this clone cannot be taken for. What
 * hands it to `git worktree add` fetches that copy first.
 */
export function publishedBase(branch: string): string {
  return `${ON_ORIGIN}${branch}`
}

/** The branch's name a {@link publishedBase} is of, as a person reads it; nothing for a base that is a branch of this clone. */
export function publishedBranch(base: string): string | undefined {
  return base.startsWith(ON_ORIGIN) ? base.slice(ON_ORIGIN.length) : undefined
}

I traced both paths from the dashboard down to the `claude` and `codex` processes. All paths below are relative to `/Users/suleiman/Projects/openagent/.branches/agent-2026-11-21T17-50-08-691Z/`. Today a user message is a single string the whole way down.

Three things matter most for images:
- **No project `start` hook line any more.** The daemon calls this computer's run host (`localHost`) directly.
- **Two drivers.** Claude Code already uses `--input-format stream-json`, so it can take image content blocks. Codex uses `codex app-server` with `input: [{type:'text',…}]`, where `{type:'localImage', path}` items can go.
- **Process hops use command-line arguments and environment variables only.** There are two hops: daemon → detached `agent-runner` process, then runner → agent CLI. Neither uses JSON or a file for the prompt, and the detached runner gets no stdin.

| Place | Path | Shared or synced? | What's there |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run's live directory | `<checkout>/.openagent/` (checkout = `<repo>/.branches/<branch>/`, or `~/.openagent-sessions/<id>/` for a session with no project) | Local, git-ignored with `*`. Removed with the checkout when it's reclaimed. | `<id>.json`, `<id>.jsonl`, `<id>.live`, `inbox.jsonl` |
| Project root `.openagent/` | `<repo>/.openagent/` (`agent-data/src/names.ts:43`, "OpenAgent's own files on this machine") | Local, hidden by its own ignore file | Project presets and similar |
| Runner directory | `<repo>/.agent-runner/` (`engine/names.ts`: `RUNNER_DIR`; `runs/<id>.lock`, `runs/<id>.stderr`, `config.yml`; `run-lock.ts:32/36`) | Local, hidden from git | Locks, stderr, machine config |
| Personal folder | `~/.openagent`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openagent` (`agent-data/src/personal-folder.ts:22`) | **A git repo, committed whole and synced** to the person's remote when one is set | `projects/<projectKey>/` (each project's run records unless shared, `project-data.ts:36/60`) and `sessions/` (records of sessions with no project, `sessions.ts:13`) |
| `agent-data` branch | `<repo>/.branches/agent-data` (`names.ts:19`, `project-data.ts:69`) | **Pushed to origin** when the project is shared | Records of shared projects |
| Sessions home | `~/.openagent-sessions`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openagent-sessions` (`sessions.ts:16`) | Local. It sits beside the personal folder on purpose ("committed whole and synced… a session's folder holds its work, not its record"). | Per-session working folders |

// The dashboard's RPC surface (#405), served in-process by the daemon so `sendStart` can reach
// the daemon's own `startAgent`. The browser calls the functions of the modules below by name over
// `POST /_rpc/<name>`; the dashboard's `rpc/` modules are typed stubs against their signatures, so
// a rename that misses one is a type error rather than a 404 at runtime.
export type { LiveFeedEvent } from './events.js'

import * as reads from './reads.js'
import * as control from './control.js'
import * as projects from './projects.js'
import * as preferences from './preferences.js'
import * as quota from './quota.js'
import * as models from './models.js'

import * as modules from './modules.js'
import * as person from './person.js'
import * as people from './people.js'
import * as accounts from './accounts.js'
import * as logins from './logins.js'

import * as personalFolder from './personal-folder.js'
import * as projectAgentData from './project-agent-data.js'
import * as presets from './presets.js'
import * as skillChoices from './skill-choices.js'
import * as plugins from './plugins.js'
import * as backup from './backup.js'
import { streamAgentEvents } from './events.js'

/** One RPC: called with whatever the browser sent, answering with whatever JSON.stringify keeps. */
export type RpcHandler = (...args: never[]) => unknown

/**
 * Every RPC the mount will answer, by name.
 *
 * Built from the modules' own exports rather than listed by hand, so a function that is exported
 * and simply never registered — the failure that shipped per-project preferences broken (#866),
 * a 400 and nothing else — cannot happen: the name IS the export name.
 *
 * Null-prototype, because the name is a path segment off an unauthenticated request and this table
 * is indexed by it directly. With `Object.prototype` behind it, `POST /_rpc/constructor` found
 * `Object` and answered 200 with whatever it was handed, and `__proto__` / `toString` / `valueOf`
 * were reachable too — 500s rather than the 404 a name that is not an RPC has to get.
 */
export const RPC_HANDLERS: Record<string, RpcHandler> = Object.assign(
  Object.create(null) as Record<string, RpcHandler>,
  Object.fromEntries(
    [reads, control, projects, preferences, quota, models, modules, person, people, accounts, logins, personalFolder, projectAgentData, presets, skillChoices, plugins, backup]
      .flatMap(module => Object.entries(module))
      .filter((entry): entry is [string, RpcHandler] => typeof entry[1] === 'function'),
  ),
)

/** The live event stream, which is a subscription rather than a call — see `rpc-serve.ts`. */
export const RPC_EVENT_STREAM = streamAgentEvents

Updating a removed image just hits a no-op map entry, so that's fine. Then I'm checking the unmount cleanup in strict mode, where effects double-invoke in dev and the cleanup could revoke images too early.

I'm tracing the bug: after a successful start, the launcher's images stay in place, including for 'launcher:session'. The start callback navigates to the run page, which unmounts the Composer, so the `.finally` that calls `composerRef.current?.clear()` finds a null ref and never clears the draft images.

The fix is to clear the image draft at the same point the text draft is cleared, inside the start callback, so it doesn't depend on the Composer's ref still being alive. The hook's effect only writes when the names change, so it won't bring the images back, and if the Composer is still mounted the `clear()` in `.finally` covers it anyway.
The launcher kept its draft images after a start because the box was already gone when `clear()` ran, so I'm fixing it the same way the text draft is dropped.

## In the box (as asked)

- Images stand in a row above the text, inside the box, 8px apart: 120×120 tiles with 10px corners, the whole image fitted on a dark tile.

## Choices I made

**Where the images live**
- Images are kept on this computer only, in a folder of the user's beside OpenAgent's other files: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openagent-images`, else `~/.openagent-images`. The folder is mode 700 and each file 600. They never go into a run's checkout, the personal folder or a project's agent data, all of which can be pushed.
- An image is named by its content: `<sha256>.<ext>`. The same image pasted twice is kept once. A message, the run's command line, the inbox, a resume and the run's record carry only these names, never the bytes. Only the coding agent's driver reads the file, as it hands the image over.
- An image is kept as soon as it is in the box, not when the message is sent. Its tile shows the file read in the browser right away, with a spinner until it is kept.
- The dashboard serves a kept image at `/_rpc/images/<name>`, behind the same origin and Host guards as every call. It answers by name only, and caches for good since the name is the content.

**What the agent gets**
- Each coding agent gets the images in its own way:
  - The first gets them as image blocks before the words of the same user message, also for a message handed over mid-turn.
  - The second gets each image's file path as a local-image input before the words, also for a message handed over mid-turn.

This testing found a bug, now fixed and tested: after a start, the launcher's draft kept its images.

- Images are kept in `~/.openagent-images`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openagent-images` if that's set. They're readable by you only and named by their content's hash. Everything else passes these names around; only the agent's driver reads the file.

- A message still needs words: an image alone doesn't send.
- A paste that carries text as well as a picture is treated as text, so copying from a web page doesn't attach a rendering of it.
- Images never leave this computer, so a start or message with images to a run on another host is refused, with a message saying why.

Yes. This branch is already built in its worktree. Run its dashboard on its own port, because typing `openagent` while your usual one is on 4200 just hands over to that one.

**1. Start it from a scratch repository, with its own config folder** so your projects and settings aren't shared:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/img-try/project && cd /tmp/img-try/project
git init -q && echo hi > README.md && git add . && git commit -qm init
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/img-try/cfg node ~/Projects/openagent/.branches/agent-2026-11-21T17-50-08-691Z/packages/dashboard/dist/bin.js --port 4317
```

It opens http://127.0.0.1:4317/project in your browser, with the scratch repository already added as a project.

**2. Things to try:**
- **Paste:** press ⌃⇧⌘4 to copy a screenshot of part of your screen, click in the box, then ⌘V. A tile should appear above the text.
- **Drag:** drag an image file from Finder onto the box. Its edge lights up while you drag.
- **Remove:** hover a tile to see the X, then click it.
- **View large:** click a tile; close it with X, Esc, or a click beside the image.
- **Start a session:** paste an image, then type something like "What word is in this screenshot?" and press Enter. A real agent run starts.
- **Follow-up:** once the agent answers, paste another image in the session's box and send it.
- **Reload:** the chat should still show each message's images. An image left unsent in the box should stay there after a reload too.
- **Edge cases:**
  - Paste text copied from a web page: it should go in as text, not as an image.
  - Drop a `.txt` file: a note should say only images go with a message.
  - Drop a HEIC photo: its tile should say the agent can't read that kind.

**3. Afterwards:** stop it with Ctrl+C, then `rm -rf /tmp/img-try`. The images are in `/tmp/img-try/cfg/openagent-images`, so they go with it.

If you'd rather try it on your real projects, stop your dashboard on 4200 and run the same `node …/bin.js` command without `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `--port`. Images then go to `~/.openagent-images`.

For a free offline walk-through instead, run `pnpm demo` in the worktree. The scripted agent there only answers `done: <prompt>`, so it shows the box and the chat but can't actually read the image.
